free_tier.stated: No free trial, stated in the provider's own words on two pages, while a third page offers three days of free access and the refund documentation invites a request to discuss free testing, so the provider publishes two answers at once. What is real is hourly billing on every virtual server: the machine is charged from delivery to cancellation, so a few hours of a full machine cost a few roubles and the unused remainder of a month returns to the balance as credit rather than as money. The cheapest shape is vm.v2-pico at 1 vCPU, 1 GB RAM, 40 GB SSD, a 1 Gbit/s port and 3 TB of traffic included, for RUB 490 a month.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: Hourly billing is the composition this provider offers: at RUB 490 a month a machine costs about RUB 0.67 an hour, so the whole catalogue can be benchmarked for the price of a coffee, and 3 TB of included traffic on a 1 Gbit/s port is the cheapest per-terabyte allowance found at RUB 163 a terabyte.

limits.value: The included traffic is the first thing to fail at a user's volume: 3 TB a month is about 100 GB a day, and the port at 1 Gbit/s could move thirty times that, so the allowance rather than the link is the ceiling.

identity_cost.detail: payment is in roubles by Russian bank cards including Mir, by bank transfer and by electronic payment systems, so a card is one accepted rail rather than a stated requirement; there is no free tier to gate. The record does not state whether signup asks for an email, a phone or an ID document, whether a card issued outside Russia works — its notes say the payment page names Mir and Russian transfers only — or any hold, debit or prepaid answer

notes: The three-day claim on the marketing page is not a contract and is contradicted twice on the same domain, so a reader should treat it as copy rather than as an offer. Arithmetic: 490 / 730 = 0.67 RUB an hour; 490 / 3 = 163 RUB a terabyte. Not established: which of the two trial statements is honoured in practice, since that needs an account and a support conversation, and whether foreign cards work (the payment page names Mir and Russian transfers only).
